title: IT Officer in Public-Sector Banks (IBPS SO)

value.body: IT Officer (Scale I) is one of the specialist officer posts that public-sector banks fill through the IBPS Specialist Officers (SO) exam. IT officers look after a bank's core banking systems, networks, information security, data centres and digital channels. Some banks, such as SBI, also advertise their own specialist IT posts outside IBPS.

items.label: Grade
items.note: Junior Management Grade Scale I officer

items.label: Basic pay scale
items.note: Plus DA, HRA and other allowances

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A four-year engineering/technology degree in Computer Science, IT, Computer Applications, Electronics or related branches, or a postgraduate degree in these subjects (MCA, M.Sc CS/IT). A three-year B.Sc or BCA alone usually does not qualify unless paired with a postgraduate degree or a NIELIT (DOEACC) 'B' level qualification — check the current notice. IBPS notifies the SO exam about once a year: an online prelims, a mains professional-knowledge test and an interview.

value.title: At a glance
items: Vacancies are shared across six specialist posts, are provisional, and the IT officer count changes every year.
Postings can be anywhere in the bank's network, and transfers are part of the job.
Much of the work is running and securing the bank's systems and managing vendor-built software, rather than building products from scratch.
Promotions follow the bank's internal promotion policy, as for other officers.
